Everyday care

Care in the chair.
Confidence at home.

A cleaning appointment is an opportunity to ask about plaque, areas that are difficult to reach and the tools your dental professional recommends. The approach will depend on your assessment.

Daily brushing and cleaning between your teeth still matter between visits. Tell the team which parts of your routine are difficult so you can work through practical changes together.

Plan a visit
What to expect

A clear path through your visit.

  1. 01Review your routine.

    Talk about the products you use, sensitive areas and anything that makes daily care difficult.

  2. 02Discuss your cleaning.

    Your clinician can explain the proposed approach and answer questions before starting.

  3. 03Make home care manageable.

    Ask for a demonstration and recommendations that fit your own teeth and gums.

Make room for your questions

Ask the things
that matter to you.

You deserve to understand the recommendation before choosing what happens next. These questions can help start the conversation.

  • What will the cleaning involve for me?
  • Which areas need more attention at home?
  • What should I expect after the appointment?
A few helpful answers

Before your visit.

A little preparation can make the next conversation feel easier.

All your questions, answered
Does a cleaning replace brushing?

No. Professional care supports your daily routine. Continue the home-care approach recommended by your dentist or hygienist.

What if my teeth are sensitive?

Mention sensitivity before the appointment. The clinician can discuss what might help and whether further assessment is needed.

How often do I need a cleaning?

The timing depends on your assessment and oral health needs. Ask your dental professional to explain their recommendation.
